regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Advanced salivary gland cancer, after specialist review of histology, treatment choices and goals.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cyclophosphamide is activated in the body into compounds that damage DNA. Bladder irritation is one reason for a clear hydration plan. Doxorubicin interacts with DNA and topoisomerase II, disrupting copying and repair. Its heart and tissue effects require particular care. Cisplatin forms links within DNA that impede copying. The kidneys, hearing and nerves can also be affected.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Doxorubicin 50 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² on Day 1, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles, stopping earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects.
key_points: Doxorubicin 50 mg/m², cisplatin 50 mg/m² and cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² on Day 1, repeated every 21 days for up to 6 cycles, stopping earlier for progression or unacceptable side effects.

Full blood count, kidney and liver tests during treatment. Review hydration, blood salts, hearing, tingling or numbness, heart symptoms, mouth care and prior toxicities before further doses. Record lifetime anthracycline exposure; the source doxorubicin limit is 450 mg/m².

Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.

cells: Full blood count, kidney and liver tests and ECG. Heart-pumping assessment with an echo or MUGA scan if over 65 or clinically indicated; doxorubicin requires LVEF above 50%. Hearing assessment and measured kidney clearance when indicated.

Full blood count, kidney and liver tests during treatment. Review hydration, blood salts, hearing, tingling or numbness, heart symptoms, mouth care and prior toxicities before further doses. Record lifetime anthracycline exposure; the source doxorubicin limit is 450 mg/m².
Extra tests may be needed for symptoms, dehydration or abnormal results.
Review results, recovery and previous toxicity before any restart or next dose.
The team reviews the cancer, side effects and your preferences. Scans follow your individual treatment plan; this regimen does not set one universal scan interval.

rows.label: Appointments and medicines
cells: Agree the treatment aim, dose and complete medicines list.

Doxorubicin is given slowly into a vein over about 15 minutes, cisplatin over 2 hours, then cyclophosphamide over 30 minutes. Cisplatin requires prescribed intravenous fluids before and after treatment, so the visit takes longer than the drug infusion times. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, swelling or leakage around the line.
Keep a current dose and symptom record.

Follow the unit’s cisplatin hydration plan and individual fluid target. The source advises 2–3 litres on Day 1 to reduce bladder irritation from cyclophosphamide; the team must adapt this if heart or kidney problems restrict fluids. Report blood in urine or painful urination promptly.
Keep follow-up and recovery checks even after the last dose.

Confirm the booked test dates with your team.

priority_toxicities: Low blood counts, infection, bleeding and anaemia
Sickness, mouth ulcers, diarrhoea, tiredness and hair loss
Doxorubicin-related heart damage and tissue injury if it leaks outside a vein
Cisplatin-related kidney damage, low blood salts, hearing loss and nerve damage
Cyclophosphamide-related bladder irritation and blood in urine
Fertility effects, pregnancy risk and rare later second cancers

regimen_profiles.regimen_role: Recurrent or advanced head and neck cancer
regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: This treatment aims to slow cancer growth and help control symptoms. Your team explains the expected benefit, uncertainty and alternatives for your situation.
regimen_profiles.treatment_setting: Recurrent, advanced or metastatic head and neck squamous cell cancer in people with comorbidities or unsuitable for combination chemotherapy.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Methotrexate interferes with folate-dependent reactions that cells need to make DNA. This can slow cancer-cell division, while also affecting blood-cell production and the lining of the mouth and bowel.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Methotrexate 40 mg/m² by intravenous bolus on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. There is no scheduled Day-22 dose. The clinician may increase to 50 mg/m² only if there has been no mucositis.
key_points: Methotrexate 40 mg/m² by intravenous bolus on Days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle, until progression or unacceptable toxicity. There is no scheduled Day-22 dose. The clinician may increase to 50 mg/m² only if there has been no mucositis.

Repeat blood count, kidney and liver tests and urinalysis; examine the mouth and throat for mucosal changes during treatment. The team confirms the test timing before each planned dose and reviews recovery and previous dose delays.

Tell the pharmacist about all painkillers, antibiotics, supplements and other medicines because interactions can increase methotrexate toxicity. Report new cough or breathlessness, mouth ulcers, unusual bleeding, jaundice, reduced urine or severe rash promptly.

Follow the unit’s mouth-care plan. Report pain, poor intake or weight loss early; ask for dietetic support. Pace activity, rest and work around symptoms.
